title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues Grothendieck's bookkeeping of the big diagram (62) of profinite groups attached to a pair (rho, sigma). The setting is the 'équation des lacets' part of the Longue Marche sequel, i.e. Teichmüller/Galois-type groups.

The previous page set up the notation:
- gamma_{rho,sigma} is a terminal quotient group, and all groups X in the diagram map to it by delta_X.
- chi_X = chi_gamma o delta_X : X -> Z^hat^* is a cyclotomic-type character.
- epsilon_{X,rho} and epsilon_{X,sigma} : X -> {±1} are two sign characters.
- Kernels: X^+ = Ker chi_X, X' = Ker epsilon_{X,rho}, X'' = Ker epsilon_{X,sigma}, X^0 = X' ∩ X'', and SX = Ker delta_X.

First paragraph (end of f). Let epsilon_𝔊 be the common sign character of the subgroup 𝔊 (the commutativity in (66) makes the two signs agree on 𝔊). Its kernel is exactly 𝔊^+, the kernel of chi restricted to 𝔊. Moreover, 𝔊 can be described as a subgroup of M_{rho,sigma} or of G_{rho,sigma}: it is the inverse image of the order-2 subgroup {1, tau'_Gamma} of Gamma_{rho,sigma} (resp. {1, tau'_gamma} of gamma_{rho,sigma}). Here tau' in 𝔊 is an involution, presumably a 'complex-conjugation'-like element. So 𝔊 is the full preimage of a Z/2 generated by the image of tau', and 𝔊^+ is the index-2 part where the character is trivial.

Part g). The core of (62) is diagram (67). Four groups surject onto gamma_{rho,sigma}: Z_{rho,sigma}, N^+_rho, N^+_sigma and G_{rho,sigma}. From these one forms iterated fibre products over gamma for certain subsets of the four. Together with gamma itself (the empty fibre product), this gives 9 groups. The initial term is SoM_{rho,sigma}, the fibre product of all four. The characters to Z^hat^* and {±1}, {±1} are bracketed as auxiliary, and 𝔊 and 𝔊^+ are attached by dotted arrows.

Taking the kernels of the maps to gamma turns this into a diagram of the same combinatorial shape (continued on the next page). Its vertices are:
- the kernels L_0 = SZ, SN^*_rho, SN^*_sigma and G^+ = SG;
- products of these, since the kernel of a fibre product over gamma is the product of the kernels;
- {1}, the kernel of the identity, as the empty product.
The arrows are the canonical projections.

This is a standard and correct observation about fibre products of groups over a common quotient. The page is organisational: it fixes notation and the shape of a lattice of fibre products in preparation for the main computations.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The count 'huit' in the machine transcription is spurious: the image has 'quatre' struck through and 'neuf' written, consistent with 9 = empty + 4 singletons + 3 intermediate + 1 total fibre product.

One small gap: why exactly 3 intermediate fibre products (rather than all 11 non-trivial subsets) is not justified on the page. It is presumably dictated by which fibre products occur naturally in (62).

ideas.what: The kernel of a fibre product of groups over a common quotient is the product of the kernels; hence the lattice of fibre products over gamma maps to an isomorphic-shape lattice of products of kernels.
ideas.modern_name: fibre products of groups / Goursat-type bookkeeping

ideas.what: The subgroup 𝔊 is the preimage of the order-2 subgroup generated by the image of an involution tau' (complex-conjugation-like). The kernel of its sign character equals the kernel of its cyclotomic character.
ideas.modern_name: extended (orientation-reversing) mapping class / Teichmüller-type groups with complex conjugation; GT-type cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Longue Marche); later Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) treats related groups; this specific notation is unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: The page is purely notational and organisational: it describes the shape of a diagram of fibre products and their kernels. It contains no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'L'image de ε𝔊 est la même que 𝔊^+' should read 'Le noyau de ε_𝔊 n'est autre que 𝔊^+.'
'En fait comme sous-groupe' should read 'En fait, en tant que sous-groupe'.
'le terme initial étant 𝔊_0 M_{rho,sigma}' should read 'le terme initial étant SoM_{rho,sigma}'.
'en ne comptant pas 𝔊 [...]^+ envoyés par ... deux flèches pointillées' is likely 'en ne comptant pas 𝔊, 𝔊^+ insérés par les deux flèches pointillées'.

'En prenant les images des huit [?] de ces neuf groupes' should read 'En prenant les noyaux des flèches de ces neuf groupes dans gamma_{rho,sigma}'. Here 'quatre' is struck and replaced by 'neuf', and 'noyaux' is consistent with the next page's kernel description.
